context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. It ensures strict cross-border health data residency and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients (Mobile and Web clients)
- Clinicians (Web clients)
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (GCP instances in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- External Pharmacies (EU national e-prescription networks and US pharmacy networks)
- Identity Providers (OAuth2/OIDC)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to Platform: HTTPS, WebRTC, OIDC (authentication/video/data mgmt)
- Platform to External Pharmacies: mTLS, HL7 FHIR (US), national e-prescription standards (EU via REST/SOAP)
- Platform to Identity Providers: OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce data residency
- Protocols: HTTPS, TLS 1.3, mTLS, WebRTC with global TURN/STUN relay servers
- Standards: HL7 FHIR (US), national e-prescription standards (EU)
- Security & Storage: AES-256 for data-at-rest, OAuth2/OIDC, append-only ledgers for AI audit logs

## Rationale
Regionally isolated GCP instances enforce strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance while maintaining localized data residency. Distributed WebRTC relays and cryptographic audit logging satisfy rural availability and EU MDR traceability constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA requirements.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Web & Mobile Frontend Applications (Flutter/React)
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud API Gateway)
- Consultation Service with WebRTC SFU (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python/FastAPI)
- E-Prescription & Interoperability Service (Node.js/Java)
- Data Storage Layer (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL + Cloud Storage)
- External Pharmacies and Identity Providers

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS (REST/JSON) and WSS (WebSockets)
- API Gateway to Microservices via gRPC over mTLS
- Microservices to Data Storage via SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres
- E-Prescription Service to External Pharmacies via HL7 FHIR (US) and national standards (EU)

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for regional data residency
- Cloud Service Mesh & SPIFFE/SPIRE: Enforces secure internal mTLS communication
- Cloud KMS / Cloud HSM: Provides regional CMEK and digital signing for non-repudiation
- OpenTelemetry: Handles distributed tracing with edge PII/PHI scrubbing

## Rationale
Isolating containers and datastores within regional GCP zones guarantees compliance with GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates. Using gRPC over mTLS and WebRTC SFU ensures secure, low-latency, and resilient communication for unstable rural networks.

Web & Mobile Frontend Applications.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-Border Telehealth Platform delivering video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict cross-border compliance while supporting unstable rural internet connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Clinicians (Users)
- Web & Mobile Frontend Applications (Flutter / React Unified Container)
- UI Router & State Management Component
- Video Consultation Module (WebRTC / Flutter WebRTC)
- AI Symptom Checker UI Component
- Patient Consent Dashboard Component
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud API Gateway)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web & Mobile Frontend Applications: Interacts with the platform [HTTPS, WSS]
- Video Consultation Module -> API Gateway: Streams media and signaling [WSS / WebRTC DTLS/SRTP]
- AI Symptom Checker UI -> API Gateway: Submits symptoms and receives traceable model outputs [HTTPS / REST]
- Patient Consent Dashboard -> API Gateway: Submits granular consent preferences [HTTPS / REST]

## Technology Stack
- Flutter / React: Unified codebase for cross-platform web and mobile support without maintaining separate binaries.
- WebRTC / Flutter WebRTC: Handles real-time media streams and adaptive bitrate control for low-bandwidth rural connections.
- OAuth2/OIDC with OIDC Tenant Discovery: Secures authentication and runtime region-locking for session data residency.
- SSL/TLS Certificate Pinning & RASP: Protects mobile clients against MITM attacks and compromised devices.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a unified client codebase with runtime region discovery to maintain user accessibility while strictly enforcing regional data residency. Client-side adaptive video modules and security controls directly satisfy rural availability and medical compliance requirements.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using GCP infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Clinicians (Users)
- External Pharmacies & Identity Providers (External Systems)
- Web & Mobile Frontend Applications (Flutter / React)
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud API Gateway)
- Consultation Service (Go, WebRTC SFU)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- E-Prescription & Interoperability Service (Node.js / Java)
- Data Storage Layer (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL + Cloud Storage)
- GCP Global HTTP(S) Load Balancer & Cloud Armor

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Frontend -> GCP Global Load Balancer: Ingress traffic [HTTPS/REST, WSS]
- GCP Global Load Balancer -> API Gateway: Regional ingress traffic [HTTPS]
- API Gateway -> Consultation Service: Routes consultation requests [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Gateway -> AI Symptom Checker Service: Routes symptom checking requests with W3C Trace Context [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Gateway -> E-Prescription & Interoperability Service: Routes e-prescription requests [gRPC over mTLS]
- Auth Component -> External Identity Providers: Token validation [OIDC/JWKS over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider:** GCP (regions: europe-west3, us-central1) for strict data residency compliance (GDPR/HIPAA).
- **API Gateway:** Envoy managed via Google Cloud API Gateway for edge routing, rate limiting, and TLS 1.3 termination.
- **Load Balancing:** GCP Global HTTP(S) Load Balancer with Cloud Armor and Regional NEGs to prevent cross-border data leaks.
- **Communication Protocols:** gRPC over mTLS for secure internal service communication; WSS for client signaling.
- **Observability:** Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus and regional Cloud Logging buckets for PII-redacted audit trails.

## Rationale
The multi-region GCP deployment guarantees that EU patient data remains in `europe-west3` and US data in `us-central1`, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Offloading heavy media tunneling to the Consultation Service while using Envoy for edge routing and load shedding ensures system availability and low latency for rural users.

Consultation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Consultation Service container provides real-time video consultations for a cross-border telehealth platform operating in the EU and US. It ensures low-bandwidth reliability and compliance with data residency and privacy regulations.

## Key Elements
* Signaling Component (Go, WebSockets): Manages WebRTC connection setup and room coordination.
* SFU Media Router (Go, Pion WebRTC): Handles media mixing and routing with adaptive bitrate control.
* Session Management Component (Go): Enforces access control, checks patient consent, and logs session metadata.
* Bandwidth Adaptator Component (Go): Dynamically monitors stream metrics and triggers downscaling for degraded mode.
* Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Compute-optimized (C2/C3) instance pools running in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
* Global TURN/STUN Relay Nodes: Managed via Google Cloud Load Balancers for NAT traversal.

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Signaling Component: Routes consultation requests [gRPC over mTLS]
* Signaling Component -> SFU Media Router: Manages media tracks [In-process / Go function calls]
* Signaling Component -> Session Management Component: Validates auth tokens [In-process]
* Bandwidth Adaptator Component -> SFU Media Router: Adjusts track bitrates dynamically [In-process / Go channels]
* Session Management Component -> Data Storage Layer: Persists regional session states [SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres]
* SFU Media Router -> Client Applications: Relays encrypted video/audio [DTLS-SRTP]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for high concurrency and low-footprint in-process threading.
* Pion WebRTC: Enables pure-Go media routing and low-latency stream adaptation.
* PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL): Provides secure, region-bound relational storage.
* GKE & Google Cloud Load Balancers: Support auto-scaling and global traffic distribution.

## Rationale
This architecture uses in-process Go components and Pion WebRTC to minimize latency and meet the <300 kbit/s degraded mode requirement for rural users. Regional GKE clusters and token-based TURN relays enforce strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints.

AI Symptom Checker Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and EU MDR traceability.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud API Gateway)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- API Controller Component
- Inference Orchestrator Component
- Audit & Compliance Logger Component
- Response Formatting & Disclaimer Engine Component
- Data Storage Layer (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL + WORM Cloud Storage)
- Vertex AI Model Registry

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> API Controller: Routes symptom checking requests [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Controller -> Inference Orchestrator: Delegates pseudonymized analysis [In-memory]
- Inference Orchestrator -> Audit & Compliance Logger: Emits prediction audit events [Async Pub/Sub]
- Inference Orchestrator -> Response Formatting & Disclaimer Engine: Passes raw triage output [In-memory]
- Response Formatting & Disclaimer Engine -> API Controller: Returns compliant payload [In-memory]
- Audit & Compliance Logger -> Data Storage Layer: Writes immutable logs [SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres & WORM Storage]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency constraints.
- Python / FastAPI: Powers the AI Symptom Checker microservice.
- Vertex AI Model Registry: Manages model versioning, cryptographic signing, and auditability.
- GCP Cloud Storage (Bucket Lock): Implements WORM storage for immutable audit logs.
- OpenTelemetry: Provides distributed tracing for latency SLO enforcement (<2s p95).

## Rationale
Regional deployments and decoupled storage guarantee strict compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR. Asynchronous logging and optimized processing components maintain high availability and low latency for rural users.

E-Prescription & Interoperability Servic.analysis:
## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The E-Prescription & Interoperability Service manages prescription lifecycles, regional format translations, and secure pharmacy dispatch.]

## Key Elements
- Prescription Orchestrator Component
- US FHIR Adapter Component
- EU National Gateway Adapter Component
- Prescription Status & Audit Component
- Google Cloud Pub/Sub
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL
- GCP KMS & Cloud Storage WORM

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Prescription Orchestrator: Invokes prescription creation [gRPC]
- Prescription Orchestrator -> US FHIR Adapter / EU Gateway Adapter: Delegates payload transformation [Internal Java Interfaces]
- US FHIR Adapter / EU Gateway Adapters -> External Pharmacies: Dispatches messages [HTTPS, REST, HL7 FHIR over mTLS]
- US FHIR Adapter / EU Gateway Adapters -> Prescription Status & Audit: Publishes delivery status updates [Google Cloud Pub/Sub]
- Prescription Status & Audit -> Data Storage Layer: Persists audit logs and status changes [SSL-enforced TCP, PostgreSQL]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Enterprise integration and robust ecosystem support for adapters
- Resilience4j: Circuit breakers for handling external pharmacy downtime
- Google Cloud Pub/Sub: At-least-once asynchronous event delivery with partition ordering
- GCP KMS: Envelope encryption for secure data-at-rest and event payload protection
- Cloud Storage WORM: Tamper-resistant immutable audit logging

## Rationale
[This modular, event-driven architecture guarantees region-specific data residency (EU/US) while ensuring zero prescription loss through Dead Letter Queues and durable messaging. Pluggable regional adapters and strict mTLS integration provide the necessary compliance, security, and interoperability required for cross-border healthcare delivery.]

Data Storage Layer.analysis:
## Overview
A secure, region-isolated Data Storage Layer built on GCP ensures strict compliance with GDPR and HIPAA for cross-border telehealth operations. It provides persistent storage, consent tracking, and traceable AI logs across European and US deployments.

## Key Elements
- EU Data Store: Deployed in `europe-west3` (`eu-postgresql` and `eu-bucket`)
- US Data Store: Deployed in `us-central1` (`us-postgresql` and `us-bucket`)
- Clinical Database (`Cloud SQL PostgreSQL`): Stores structured PHI/PII and e-prescriptions using Row-Level Security
- Consent & Audit Engine (`PostgreSQL Schema/Triggers`): Maintains immutable audit logs and granular consent states
- Blob Storage Repository (`Cloud Storage`): Handles unstructured media and raw AI payloads via regional buckets
- Data Access Proxy (`Envoy / Sidecar`): Intercepts traffic to inject regional context and validate client certificates
- PgBouncer: Manages connection pooling for high availability during peak hours

## Relationships
- Consultation Service -> Data Storage Layer: Reads and writes consultation data [SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres via mTLS]
- AI Symptom Checker Service -> Data Storage Layer: Reads and writes symptom check data and model versions [SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres]
- E-Prescription & Interoperability Service -> Data Storage Layer: Reads and writes prescription data [SSL-enforced TCP/Postgres]
- Data Access Proxy -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Routes regional traffic and injects session context [Local TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Selected for relational data management with native Row-Level Security (RLS) support.
- Cloud Storage: Chosen for secure, region-isolated unstructured media and audit log retention.
- Cloud KMS: Implemented for Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) to enforce regional data encryption.
- Envoy / Sidecar & mTLS: Utilized for secure zero-trust service-to-database communication and client certificate verification.
- PgBouncer: Deployed for connection pooling and overload protection during traffic bursts.

## Rationale
This architecture physically separates EU and US health data into distinct GCP regions to guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance. Dedicated security controls, immutable audit logging, and localized backups ensure regulatory traceability without sacrificing system availability or performance.
